## Purpose and scope

This protocol extracts genomic DNA from soil microarthropods preserved in 96% ethanol, using spin columns (NZY Tissue gDNA Isolation Kit). It is the manual alternative to the robot extraction (EnGeL-MOLB-DNA-MAG), for smaller batches. Specimens are homogenised, so the method is destructive: specimens cannot be archived afterwards. Two homogenisation options are given: manual pestle grinding and mechanical bead beating.

## Principle

Ethanol is removed by centrifugation, pipetting and evaporation. Specimens are homogenised and digested with Proteinase K in Buffer NT1. After lysis, Buffer NL and ethanol adjust the conditions so that DNA binds to the silica membrane of a spin column. Two wash buffers remove contaminants, the membrane is dried, and DNA is eluted in preheated Buffer NE (NZYtech, NZY Tissue gDNA Isolation Kit).

## Reagent preparation

- **Buffer NW2:** add ethanol before first use, as stated on the bottle [TO CONFIRM: volume for the kit size].
- **Buffer NE:** preheat to 70 °C before elution.

## Procedure

### Before starting

{{< include ../../includes/_contamination-control.qmd >}}
- Include extraction blanks (no specimens) processed exactly like the samples [TO CONFIRM: number per batch].
- Record each sample's EnGeL label in the lab book and the Lab Pipeline workbook.

### Ethanol removal

{{< include ../../includes/_ethanol-removal.qmd >}}

### Homogenisation and lysis

(@) Add 180 µL of Buffer NT1 to each tube containing the dried microarthropods.
(@) Homogenise the specimens [TO CONFIRM: steps for both options]: (a) manual grinding with a pestle in the tube; or (b) bead beating with corundum sand and ceramic beads [TO CONFIRM: amounts, instrument, speed and time].
(@) Add 25 µL of Proteinase K to each tube.
(@) Incubate in a ThermoMixer at 56 °C with 400 rpm for 1 h 30 min.
(@) Optional (RNA removal): add 10 µL of RNase A, mix gently and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.

### DNA purification

(@) Add 200 µL of Buffer NL to each sample. Vortex for 10 s.
(@) Add 210 µL of 96–100% ethanol. Vortex immediately.
(@) Transfer the mixture to an NZYSpin Tissue column placed in a 2 mL collection tube. Centrifuge at > 11 000 × g for 1 min. Discard the flow-through and place the column in a new collection tube.
(@) First wash: add 500 µL of Buffer NW1. Centrifuge at > 11 000 × g for 1 min. Discard the flow-through.
(@) Second wash: add 600 µL of Buffer NW2 (ethanol added). Centrifuge at > 11 000 × g for 1 min. Discard the flow-through.
(@) Optional, for samples with high inhibitor content: repeat the wash with another 600 µL of Buffer NW2.
(@) Dry the membrane: place the column back in the collection tube and centrifuge at > 14 000 × g for 3 min.
(@) Transfer the column to a clean 1.5 mL tube. Add 40 µL of Buffer NE (preheated to 70 °C) to the centre of the membrane.
(@) Incubate at room temperature for 1 min, then centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 2 min to elute the DNA.

## Calculations

Not applicable: volumes are per sample. For a batch of $n$ samples, prepare $V = v \times n \times 1.1$ of each buffer ($v$: volume per sample, µL; 1.1: 10% excess).

## Quality control

| Control | Where | Purpose | Acceptance criterion |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Extraction blanks | Each batch [TO CONFIRM: number] | Detect contamination | [TO CONFIRM] |
| Extraction positive control (mock community) | When establishing a new starting material or community | Check extraction performance | [TO CONFIRM: composition and criterion] |
| DNA purity | All extracts | A~260~/A~280~, A~260~/A~230~ (EnGeL-MOLB-NAQC) | [TO CONFIRM] |
| DNA concentration | All extracts | Fluorometry (EnGeL-MOLB-NAQC) | General rule: ≥ 10 ng/µL success; < 5 ng/µL fail; between 5 and 10 ng/µL the PCR result decides |

The PCR is the best way to evaluate whether the DNA in a sample is viable.

## Data and metadata

- **Sample labels:** EnGeL labels from the sample master data file; each DNA extract gets its own code (sample nature `DNA`), with the source sample code kept in a separate column.
- **Where:** the *Sample_Tracking* sheet of the Metabarcoding Lab Pipeline workbook and the lab book.

::: {.callout-note title="Minimum to record"}
- EnGeL sample label of the source sample and of the extract
- Extraction date, operator, homogenisation option used (pestle or bead beating)
- Kit lot number; RNase A lot (if used); deviations (extra NW2 wash, split sample)
- As in the Lab Pipeline *Sample_Tracking* sheet: Extraction_pipeline, Extraction_date, Equipment, DNA_ngul, A260/280, A260/230, Elution_vol_ul, DNA_total_ng
:::

## Safety and waste

{{< include ../../includes/_safety-general.qmd >}}

**Kit hazards** (to be confirmed by the laboratory against the NZYtech SDS):

{{< include ../../includes/_safety-guanidine.qmd >}}
- Proteinase K may cause allergy or asthma symptoms if inhaled.
{{< include ../../includes/_safety-ethanol.qmd >}}

**Waste**

{{< include ../../includes/_waste-streams.qmd >}}

For this protocol: flow-through from the columns goes to biological liquid waste (jerrican), never with bleach; used columns, tubes and tips go to biological solid waste (black bin); unused or expired kit reagents go to the red bin.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Specimens aspirated with the ethanol | Narrow tip opening | Use wide-bore tips or cut off the tip of regular tips. |
| PCR inhibition | Residual ethanol, or inhibitors in the sample | Ensure complete ethanol removal; use the optional extra NW2 wash. |
| Low DNA yield | Incomplete homogenisation or lysis | [TO CONFIRM] |
| Column blocked | Too much material | [TO CONFIRM: maximum input; split the sample] |

## Remarks

The source protocol dried the specimens in a ThermoMixer (56 °C, 400 rpm, up to 1 h) after centrifuging at 10 000 × g; this version uses the ethanol removal of EnGeL-MOLB-DNA-MAG (decided 2026-11-06). The NZYtech insect support protocol homogenises up to 50 mg of insects under liquid nitrogen; this is an option to consider for the homogenisation step [TO CONFIRM].
